To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two germline gene related cross‐reactive rheumatoid factor idiotype are frequently present in rheumatoid factor positive sera of both non‐rheumatic and rheumatoid arthritis patients, but are often lost in rheumatoid sera during the course of the disease.

1) The 17.109 cross‐reactive idiotype is present on about 30% of RFs in RA and non‐RA sera, and 2) The 6B6 cross‐reactive Id is present on about half the RFs in RA sera and on about one‐fifth of the RFs in non‐RA sera.
two germline gene related cross-reactive idiotypes of rheumatoid factor are found frequently in the polycional RF of rheumatoid arthritis as well as non-rheumatoid arthritis sera.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the autoantibody response in rheumatoid disease and with the relationship of this response to the development of the disease.
the occurrence of RF idiotype in the population and in the early phases of RA.
the molecular and genetic basis of rheumatoid factor, a marker of rheumatoid arthritis, which is also present in a significant number of non‐rheumatic individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the idiotype frequencies observed in RA are not significantly different from those in non‐RA individuals.
RFs in RA and in non‐RA are not different in terms of their idiotypes, but rather that the idiotypes may be lost as a consequence to the development of RA.

these two germline gene cross‐reactive light chain idiotypes are not specific for RA, but that their occurrence in polyclonal sera is not a normal feature, and that they are lost or diminished in RA as a consequence of diversification of the polyclonal response to the self‐antigen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

these two idiotypes are present at a high frequency in the normal population, and that their presence in the polyclonally expanded RF of RA patients may represent a normal response to the chronic inflammation of RA.
these two cross‐reactive idiotype markers are present in a substantial fraction of polyclonal RF, but are not unique to RA.

the 6B.6 and 17.109 idiotypes are present in the polyclonality of RF in the general population, but that in some RA patients these idiotypes become lost as a consequence either of somatic diversifications or of the emergence of new RF clones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two cross‐reactive germline‐derived idiotypes, which we have previously shown to be expressed on RF paraproteinas, are also frequently expressed on polyclonal RF in both RA and non‐RA sera.
these germlines are used by the polyclonal B cell population in the non‐rheumatic as well as in the RA population.
